about: The REVIEWED corpus that tools/corpus-invariant.js checks a capture against: S4 task 3.7's corpus specification. It is hand-maintained on purpose and never read from tools/capture-baseline.js. Its names are the corpus as reviewed at 5803067: the 5 golden scenarios, seeds 1-20, and the 11 targeted fixtures whose reasons are recorded at their construction sites. Each entry carries its mode and status, and golden and seed entries also carry a fingerprint of the plan under the invariant's own encoding. A change to any of this is a change to what the corpus means, and must arrive as a reviewed diff to this file: add or remove names deliberately, and regenerate fingerprints with `node tools/corpus-invariant.js pin-inputs --write`, reading the diff before committing. This file is the CONTROL composition's spec (S4 task 4.7, tools/control-corpus.json), so it does not change when task 4 adds scenarios: additions arrive as the expanded composition, under new names, with their own spec.
reviewedAtMeans: The HEAD of the working tree the review was carried out on: a starting point, NOT a provenance claim. A corpus change lands in the same commit as its reviewed spec, and a file cannot name the commit that contains it, so in general the corpus a spec describes need not exist at its reviewedAt (tools/corpus-spec-expanded.json is such a case). For this control spec it does: the control corpus is unchanged from 5803067 on, which tools/control-corpus.json records and tests/control-corpus.test.js holds by input hash. What the spec describes is enforced, not labelled -- tests/corpus-invariant.test.js holds it to the corpus at every commit that contains it. Recorded by S4 task 5.3's provenance sweep; no scenario or fingerprint changed.
